title: whatsapp_inbox._ingest_inbound_message
description: The payload of the CORE event `hub.whatsapp.message_received`, verbatim. A manifest listener has no mapping layer — the relay hands the event payload straight to the command — so this schema is not free to describe a shape of its own: it describes what `crates/server/src/inbound_poll.rs::event_payload` emits. Anything stricter than the event does not degrade a feature, it dead-letters every inbound WhatsApp message.

wa_message_id.description: Meta's `wamid.…`. It is the idempotency key of the whole inbound chain (`_event_outbox.id = wa-<wa_message_id>`), so it is the one field worth refusing the message over.

from.description: Who SPOKE, as Meta reports it — digits, NO leading `+` (`34600111222`). Since hub#1612 this is not always the customer: in the echo of what the owner answered from the WhatsApp Business app it is the shop's own number, which is why the thread is keyed by `contact` and not by this (whatsapp_inbox#66).

direction.description: `inbound` (the customer wrote) or `outbound` (the echo of what the business answered from the phone). ABSENT on a hub older than hub#1612, and then it means `inbound` — that is all such a hub could serve. Deliberately NOT an enum: the runtime forwards a value it does not recognise verbatim rather than normalising it, and refusing it here would dead-letter the message instead of showing it. The column stores whatever arrives; nothing repaints it as `inbound`.

contact.description: The number at the OTHER end — the customer in BOTH directions. It is the thread: `wa_contact_id` and the E.164 `contact_phone` a `recipient_query` grant addresses. Absent on a hub older than hub#1612, where it falls back to `from`.

source.description: `live` (traffic arriving now) or `history` (the 180-day coexistence backlog the SaaS backfilled when the number was connected). Absent means `live`. It never reaches a column: it is what tells the free-tier meter and the unread badge that a backlog message is not new traffic. Not an enum, for the same reason `direction` is not.

text.description: The body of a text message, `""` for anything else (`inbound_poll.rs::text` never returns null).

received_at.description: When the SaaS stored the message (ISO-8601). Kept for the record; the row's own clock is the runtime's `:now`, which is the one every other timestamp in this hub is ordered by.

message.description: Meta's message object, verbatim — the source of truth for anything the two convenience fields above do not cover (media, interactive replies, referrals). `null` when Meta sent nothing the SaaS could store. A scalar here is refused on purpose: it would reach Postgres as invalid JSON and blow up mid-transaction instead of at the door.
